outcomes.scope: A pre-registered held-out (FIT/TEST split) re-evaluation of all five prior generative-falsification models (M2, M3, M4, M5, M5b) on the clean parser, with habit tables built exclusively from FIT-half pages and models scored on held-out TEST-half data, under two uncertain-space treatments (S, M). This reverses the family's prior in-sample ranking (M5b best at composite 0.50) to a held-out ranking where M2 (self-citation) is best (0.69-0.74) and M4 (Stolfi template) worst (1.87-1.44); shows no model matches more than 3 of 9 real corpus properties out of sample; documents a previously unnoticed dead grid parameter in the M2 pilot's code (p_new unreachable given the branch-probability ordering, collapsing the 27-point grid to 9 effective points); and extends the cipher-advocate test with corrected five-way gates across 12 untuned cipher constructions (abbreviation x homophone count, on Latin and Culpeper), showing none jointly reproduces the manuscript's word-length/type-ratio/entropy fingerprint.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: Pilot 4 in the generative-mechanism falsification family: implements the Cardan table-and-grille device (M5a independent-column, M5b row-coupled) built from the pinned ZL3b corpus, measures composite distance against real manuscript statistics across 28 configurations plus multi-seed stability, and narrows the residual gap to two local metrics (conditional bigram entropy, word-final predictability), extending outcome-m4-template-doodler-pilot.
family_comparisons.reason: This submission directly extends the same family's own five models, same grids, and same composite metric with a pre-registered held-out re-run that materially changes the family's headline conclusion. Because it re-evaluates the identical underlying capability/result rather than introducing a distinct mechanism, it is the same outcome family, cumulatively upgraded to tier 10.

family_comparisons.existing_scope: A pre-registered, frozen-decision-rule adversarial audit of six prior generative-falsification family claims: (1) discovery and quantification that the shared corpus parser used by prior pilots leaves IVTFF markup inside ~24% of published types, requiring restatement of all headline manuscript metrics under a newly implemented clean parser (with two uncertain-space treatment variants); (2) an alphabet-confound test showing the H2|1 anomaly is robust to EVA multigraph/determinism-merge alphabet normalization but the final-glyph anomaly is alphabet-dependent (0.08-0.27 bit gap depending on glyph-identity assumptions); (3) five untuned cipher constructions applied to real Latin/Culpeper plaintexts, showing a plain verbose cipher of Latin reproduces both entropy residues and fails only a type-ratio gate calibrated to the contaminated parser count; (4) permutation-null and Currier-language/section confound analysis showing the 'neighbouring-page 2x sharing' and '30% page-private' structural claims are largely artefacts of language/section confounding and hapax richness; (5) a new medieval-orthography control (two Chaucer editions) testing whether the vocabulary-richness anomaly survives non-standardized spelling.
family_comparisons.reason: This submission vendors the audit's clean-parser and metric library verbatim as a code dependency but does not claim or duplicate any of the audit's own five credited findings. It applies that library to a new held-out evaluation of the generator models, which the audit family did not perform.
